gen-press-start-2p-gf-lexend-mega: Lexend Mega draws every line with one nib and spaces its plain sans letters wide, with a visible gap in each c. And Press Start 2P brings the pixel-stamped fun up top, while the body simply keeps its stroke unbroken.
gen-righteous-gf-lexend-peta: Righteous fills the line with chunky bowls and curves that look like thin steel rod bent into shape. Lexend Peta, a plain sans, keeps its stroke uniform and its wide-mouthed c shapes easy to follow paragraph after paragraph.
gen-tourney-gf-lexend-tera: Athletic and stretched out, Tourney cuts every stroke to one width and tracks its words wide. And Lexend Tera matches that uniform line with open curves, which is the single quality that ties the pair together.
gen-audiowide-instrument-sans: Instrument Sans keeps its stroke weight constant and points the ends of each c apart like pincers. Audiowide matches that evenness with tile-like glyphs and wide gaps, and that shared flatness is the strongest thing the pair has.
gen-eater-inter: Aggressive in mood, Eater spaces its letters wide and pairs moderately weighty stems with thin strokes beside them. Inter keeps a smooth tube-like line.
gen-gf-love-ya-like-a-sister-gf-lexend-z: Ascenders that barely clear the x-height give Love Ya Like A Sister a low, level, bold stance across the line. Lexend Zetta echoes it with constant strokes.
gen-gf-revalia-gf-montserrat-alternates: Revalia sets a tall band of widely spaced letters with an open-curved g and short stalks above. And Montserrat Alternates answers its relaxed stride with wire-bent curves that never thin, a plain sans that crowds toward the capital line.
gen-gf-funnel-display-gf-lexend-giga: Lexend Giga is flat, single-weight sans-serif linework with generous tracking that opens each word. Funnel Display brings spaghetti-like strokes of the same width, so the two sit side by side as relaxed, confident cousins.
gen-gf-goldman-gf-julius-sans-one: Wide, bold, and a bit commanding, Goldman puts big lowercase forms and parenthesis-like rounds up front. Julius Sans One, a sans-serif with constant strokes and lots of blank space between letters, is the quiet counterweight.
gen-gf-grandstander-gf-lexend-mega: Grandstander's constant-width lines keep its letters held open, with short ascenders and a tall x-height that feel bold and playful. Give Lexend Mega a slightly smaller size.
